notes: §1985:VI.5.7.4 GR2 assigns level-number 77 to "noncontiguous working storage data items, noncontiguous linkage data items", usable "only as described by format 1 of the data description entry", 66 to RENAMES entries "only as described by format 2", and 88 to condition-name entries "only as described by format 3". LevelNumberPass.VisitLevelNumber refuses a level 77 under an FD or SD (COBOL1746) and passes every data description entry to CheckEntryFormat, which refuses a RENAMES body at any level but 66, a level 66 without RENAMES, a level 88 whose body is not a VALUE clause alone, and a 66, 77 or 88 entry without the name its format prints (COBOL1747); DataBinder.BindEntries refuses a level 02-49 entry that follows a level 77, so a 77 is never subdivided (COBOL2771). None of this has an edition arm. The 1985 arm is what 2002 added to those formats: the local-storage section (the third home of a 77) and the level-88 validation format, WHEN SET TO FALSE and IN alphabet-name phrases are each refused at --std 85 with COBOL0900 (VisitValueClauseFalsePhrase and its sibling gates; probed under row 1985-GR-VI.5.3.4-2). The witness declares a level 77 and a level 88 and uses both; 15 probes covered a 77 with a subordinate entry, without PICTURE, unnamed, with RENAMES, in the file section, a 66 with PICTURE or without a name, RENAMES at level 05, and the legal forms (77 in working-storage and linkage, 77 with an 88, 66 with and without THRU).

next.reason: 1985: level 77 identifies 'noncontiguous working storage data items, noncontiguous linkage data items' (format 1 only); 66 for RENAMES (format 2 only); 88 for condition-names, 'used only as described by format 3'. §2023:13.18.33.4 GR2 keeps 66 and 77 and adds 'noncontiguous local storage data items' to 77, and 88 now also defines 'criteria to be used to validate a data item' and 'may be used only as described by the condition-name format or the validation format'. §2023:8.5.1.3.2 restates the 66/77/88 assignments. The 88 restriction is loosened by the added validation format.
